concepts.def: Trying things that may be risky

walkthroughs.body_html:
Adolescence roughly ages 10-19. The body, brain and emotions all change.

The frontal lobe (planning) keeps developing well into your 20s. 🧠

Peer group friendships explode in importance.

You care more what mates think than parents — that's normal.

It also means more risk-taking, since teens often act for peer approval.

Identity = who you feel you are.

Trying out styles, hobbies, opinions is healthy.

It's also a time of independence — making your own choices. 🦋

mcqs.q: When is deception in research ever acceptable?
options: When demand characteristics would otherwise invalidate the study, with thorough debrief and ethics approval.

mcqs.q: Why does the cognitive approach use INFERENCE?
options: Mental processes cannot be directly observed, so they are inferred from behaviour.
Because cognitive psychologists guess instead of measuring.
